android-enterprise.name: Android Enterprise Foundations
android-enterprise.description: Master core deployment architectures, corporate-owned dedicated setups, OEMConfig policies, and Google Play integration for enterprise Android fleets.

lessons.name: Module 1: Architecture & Device Enrollment
lessons.summary: Understand Google Mobile Services (GMS), device management API architecture, DPC roles, and Zero-Touch staging.

details.overview: Android Enterprise utilizes a modern device management architecture built around Google Mobile Services (GMS) and the Device Policy Controller (DPC). Unlike legacy Device Administrator APIs (deprecated in Android 10), Android Enterprise uses containerization, cryptographic work boundaries, and system-level management intents to enforce enterprise policy without compromising user privacy.
topics: Evolution from legacy Device Admin to Android Enterprise Architecture
Role of Google Play EMM API & Android Management API (AMAPI)
Device Policy Controller (DPC) lifecycle and on-device token handshakes
Zero-Touch Enrollment (ZTE) portal bindings and cloud staging tokens
lab_guide: Step 1: In the EMM console, generate an enrollment QR code containing the DPC extras bundle (com.google.android.apps.work.clouddpc).
Step 2: Take a factory-reset Android 11+ endpoint and tap the initial setup "Welcome" screen 6 times to activate the system QR scanner.
Step 3: Connect to the enterprise staging Wi-Fi and allow Google Play Services to download and provision the enterprise DPC.
Step 4: Verify in adb terminal that the device owner is active using: adb shell dumpsys device_policy.
key_takeaways: Legacy Device Administrator is deprecated; all modern deployments require Android Enterprise.
Device Owner (DO) mode can only be initialized on a pristine factory-reset device prior to any accounts being added.
Zero-Touch Enrollment binds IMEI/Serial hardware hashes directly to your enterprise tenant via participating cellular carriers.

quiz.question: When can an Android device be provisioned into Device Owner (Fully Managed) mode?
options: Anytime through the device Settings menu
Only during Initial Setup wizard on a factory-reset device before any user accounts exist
Only after rooting the device operating system
By sending a broadcast SMS to the device phone number
quiz.explanation: Device Owner mode enforces system-level management and can strictly only be set up during initial out-of-box setup before any personal or corporate accounts are bound.

quiz.question: How do you activate the system camera for QR code enrollment on a newly unboxed Android device?
options: Tap the "Welcome" setup screen 6 times in the same spot
Hold the power button for 15 seconds
Swipe down twice from the notification shade
quiz.explanation: Tapping anywhere on the first setup wizard screen 6 times prompts the OS to launch its embedded QR code camera scanner.

quiz.question: Which component enforces corporate policies locally on an Android Enterprise device?
quiz.explanation: The Device Policy Controller (DPC) is the on-device client application that communicates with your EMM server and requests the OS kernel to apply security configurations.

lessons.name: Module 2: Work Profile vs Fully Managed (COBO/COPE)
lessons.summary: Deep-dive into BYOD containerization, enterprise isolation, encryption keys, and fully managed corporate restrictions.

details.overview: Android Enterprise supports distinct deployment modes tailored to device ownership. Personally-Owned (BYOD) uses a cryptographic Work Profile, establishing separate encryption keys for work and personal data. Corporate-Owned Personally-Enabled (COPE / WP-COD) provides organization-level control while preserving user privacy in a distinct container. Corporate-Owned Business-Only (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU) give IT total control over the entire device.
topics: Cryptographic user boundary isolation and separate eCryptfs/FBE storage rings
Cross-profile data sharing controls, copy/paste restrictions, and intent filters
COPE policy evolution in Android 11+ (WP-COD model)
Dedicated (COSU) kiosk appliances for POS, logistics, and digital signage
lab_guide: Step 1: Configure a Work Profile policy that restricts cross-profile copy/paste clipboard operations.
Step 2: Enroll a personal device using the Google Play work account portal link.
Step 3: Open the corporate Contacts app and verify work contacts cannot be synced or pasted into personal WhatsApp.
Step 4: Inspect running Android user spaces: adb shell pm list users.
details.commands_configs:
// Verification of dual user space in ADB
$ adb shell pm list users
Users:
  UserInfo{0:Owner:13} running
  UserInfo{10:Work profile:30} running

// Inspecting cross-profile intent filters
$ adb shell dumpsys device_policy | grep "CrossProfileIntentFilter"
key_takeaways: Work Profile uses user ID 10+ with separate hardware-backed encryption keys.
In COPE (Android 11+), IT cannot view personal apps, location, or private browsing history.
Cross-profile intent filters dictate whether corporate URLs can trigger personal browser handlers.

quiz.question: What happens to work data when a candidate resigns and an Enterprise Wipe is performed on a BYOD device?
options: The entire phone is wiped back to factory settings
Only the Work Profile container and its associated encryption keys are destroyed; personal data remains intact
The user SIM card is deactivated automatically
The device operating system is downgraded
quiz.explanation: Enterprise Wipe selectively deletes the Work Profile container and revokes its encryption keys without touching personal photos, contacts, or private apps.

quiz.question: Which deployment model is best suited for an unattended warehouse barcode scanner?
quiz.explanation: Dedicated devices (formerly COSU) are designed for single-use or kiosk scenarios where end-users should only access specific operational applications.

lessons.name: Module 3: Managed Google Play & App Distribution
lessons.summary: Set up enterprise app binding, iframe app approvals, private APK hosting, and runtime permissions configuration.

details.overview: Managed Google Play is the content marketplace and app deployment engine for Android Enterprise. IT administrators can approve public apps, upload custom enterprise line-of-business (LOB) APKs, distribute web apps, and silently push managed configurations (App Config) directly to enrolled devices without end-user interaction.
topics: Managed Google Play Enterprise account binding and Service Account credentials
Silent installation and auto-update policies over Wi-Fi only vs any network
Managed Configurations (AppConfig schema) for injecting server endpoints and credentials
Private app publishing and zero-day app rollouts
lab_guide: Step 1: Access the Managed Google Play iframe within the EMM console and search for "Google Chrome".
Step 2: Approve the app and select "Silent Auto-Install" for the Sales department device group.
Step 3: Open the Managed Configuration designer and set the Homepage URL to "https://portal.uemlabs.com".
Step 4: Grant all runtime permissions silently (CAMERA: Grant, LOCATION: Grant).
details.commands_configs:
// Sample AppConfig XML schema representation for Google Chrome
<bundle>
  <string name="HomepageLocation">https://intranet.uemlabs.com</string>
  <boolean name="IncognitoModeAvailability">1</boolean>
  <list name="URLBlocklist">
    <item>*</item>
  </list>
  <list name="URLAllowlist">
    <item>*.uemlabs.com</item>
    <item>https://login.microsoftonline.com/*</item>
  </list>
</bundle>
key_takeaways: Apps distributed via Managed Google Play update automatically through the Google Play client daemon.
Managed Configurations eliminate the need for end-users to type server URLs, usernames, or gateway settings.
Runtime permissions can be set to Automatically Grant, Automatically Deny, or Prompt User.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of AppConfig (Managed Configurations) in Android Enterprise?
options: To increase screen brightness when opening an app
To dynamically push corporate settings (URLs, tokens, flags) into an app without user entry
To decompile APK packages into Java source code
quiz.explanation: AppConfig exposes standardized XML/JSON schemas allowing administrators to pre-populate corporate endpoints, certificates, and operational flags directly into apps.

quiz.question: Can internal line-of-business (LOB) APKs be distributed privately without appearing in the public Play Store?
options: No, all apps on Google Play must be publicly accessible worldwide
Yes, via the Private Apps tab in Managed Google Play, visible only to your enterprise ID
Only by manually connecting a USB cable to each phone
Only if published under a personal Gmail account
quiz.explanation: Private Apps published through the Managed Google Play console are strictly scoped to the enterprise organization and are completely hidden from the public store.

lessons.name: Module 4: Zero-Touch Enrollment & OEMConfig
lessons.summary: Automate unboxing workflows, configure cloud carrier portals, and push OEM-specific hardware settings (Zebra, Samsung Knox).

details.overview: Zero-Touch Enrollment (ZTE) allows seamless out-of-the-box staging for corporate fleets. When an employee unboxes a new device and powers it on, the device checks the Google Zero-Touch cloud database, identifies its corporate owner, downloads the assigned EMM DPC, and applies security policies automatically. OEMConfig extends this by exposing proprietary hardware controls (barcode scanner engines, physical buttons, battery management) through standardized Play Store apps.
topics: Zero-Touch portal management and customer-reseller pairing
Configuring Zero-Touch DPC extras configuration profiles
OEMConfig architecture (Zebra OEMConfig, Samsung Knox Service Plugin, Honeywell)
Controlling hardware features: physical scanner triggers, Wi-Fi roaming thresholds
lab_guide: Step 1: Sign in to the Zero-Touch portal and link your authorized hardware reseller account.
Step 2: Create a Default Configuration mapping device IMEI numbers to your EMM server enrollment DPC.
Step 3: Approve Zebra OEMConfig in Managed Google Play and attach it to your rugged device smart group.
Step 4: Configure the physical scan button mapping to launch your enterprise inventory scanner app.
key_takeaways: Zero-Touch persists even after a hardware factory reset, preventing theft and unmanaged usage.
OEMConfig standardizes vendor-specific hardware management without waiting for EMM platform updates.
Zebra OEMConfig requires MX (Mobility Extensions) firmware version compatibility.

quiz.question: What occurs when an unauthorized user factory-resets a Zero-Touch enrolled device?
options: The device becomes an unmanaged personal phone
Upon connecting to Wi-Fi/cellular, the device re-enrolls into the corporate EMM automatically
The device enters an unrecoverable hard-brick state
The SIM card is locked with a random PUK code
quiz.explanation: Zero-Touch binds the hardware IMEI to Google servers; during initial network activation, the device detects its corporate assignment and forces corporate enrollment.

quiz.question: Which enterprise hardware management standard allows OEM vendors to expose device-specific settings through Google Play?
options: OEMConfig (built on Android Enterprise Managed Configurations)
Android Debug Bridge over public Wi-Fi
quiz.explanation: OEMConfig allows hardware OEMs (Zebra, Samsung, Honeywell) to publish schema-driven apps to Managed Google Play that expose hardware buttons, scanner tuning, and battery management directly to EMM consoles.

quiz.question: What is required to pair an enterprise customer tenant with Google Zero-Touch Enrollment?
options: Purchasing compatible Android 9+ hardware from an authorized Zero-Touch reseller who uploads device IMEIs/serials into the customer portal
Sublicensing Android OS source code from Google
Installing custom ROMs on each device
Running a local DHCP server on port 67
quiz.explanation: Zero-Touch enrollment requires hardware purchased through authorized enterprise resellers who link device hardware hashes directly to the customer organization ID.

lessons.name: Module 5: Compliance Policies & Security Rules
lessons.summary: Define password entropy, CTS profile integrity, factory reset protection, and SafetyNet / Play Integrity triggers.

details.overview: Security enforcement in Android Enterprise leverages hardware-backed attestation (Play Integrity API, formerly SafetyNet) and kernel-level SELinux policies. Administrators can enforce screen lock complexity, mandate storage encryption, prevent USB debugging, and trigger automated quarantine actions when compliance thresholds are breached.
topics: Play Integrity API checks: BASIC_INTEGRITY vs DEVICE_INTEGRITY vs STRONG_INTEGRITY
Password complexity levels: Numeric, Alphabetic, Alphanumeric, Complex Biometric
Factory Reset Protection (FRP) whitelists to prevent activation lock
Automated compliance engines: Warn, Block Access, and Selective Wipe
lab_guide: Step 1: Set up a Compliance Rule requiring Minimum OS Version 13.0 and Play Integrity Device Attestation.
Step 2: Add an action: If non-compliant for 24 hours, revoke Exchange email access and notify the security team.
Step 3: Configure corporate Google account IDs for Enterprise Factory Reset Protection override.
Step 4: Verify compliance state in the EMM device overview tab.
key_takeaways: MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY verifies the device runs a certified CTS-tested Android build with locked bootloader.
Enterprise FRP allows IT to unlock a device even if an ex-employee left their personal Google account on it.
Compliance rules should have tiered grace periods to avoid unnecessary operational disruption.

quiz.question: What does MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY in the Play Integrity API verify?
options: That the battery is charged above 80%
That the device is a genuine Android device with an unlocked custom ROM
That the device runs a certified Android build and has a locked, untampered bootloader
That the user has accepted terms of service
quiz.explanation: MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY is a cryptographic hardware attestation proving the device is running a Google-certified Android OS with a secure boot chain and locked bootloader.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of Enterprise Factory Reset Protection (FRP) in Android Enterprise?
options: To ensure IT administrators can unlock and re-provision devices even if an employee left their personal Google account on the device before departing
To format the device memory automatically every 30 days
To prevent devices from connecting to cellular towers
To disable all screen lock passcodes
quiz.explanation: Enterprise FRP whitelists specific corporate Google account IDs that are authorized to bypass activation lock following a recovery mode factory reset.

quiz.question: Which compliance tier in the Play Integrity API verifies that the endpoint is running a Google-certified Android build with a secure, locked bootloader?
quiz.explanation: MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY confirms hardware-backed cryptographic attestation that the device is running a certified OS build without unauthorized bootloader tampering or root exploits.

lessons.name: Module 6: Troubleshooting & Diagnostic Logs
lessons.summary: Capture ADB logcat, parse bug reports, trace DPC token issues, and diagnose corporate Wi-Fi authentication drops.

details.overview: Enterprise mobile engineers must know how to quickly pinpoint enrollment failures, certificate mismatches, and network drops. Android provides deep diagnostic tools through Android Debug Bridge (ADB), bugreports, dumpsys commands, and DPC diagnostic logs.
topics: Capturing and parsing Android bug reports (bugreport.zip) with Google Battery Historian / Chkbugreport
Tracing DevicePolicyManager state with adb shell dumpsys device_policy
Investigating Wi-Fi 802.1X EAP-TLS certificate failures with logcat | grep wpa_supplicant
Common enrollment error codes: 400 Bad Token, 403 Forbidden, 404 No DPC Bundle
lab_guide: Step 1: Connect endpoint via USB and authorize ADB debugging.
Step 2: Execute command to dump current device policy configurations to a text file.
Step 3: Filter logcat output for enterprise provisioning errors during a mock enrollment.
Step 4: Generate a full system bugreport using: adb bugreport enterprise_debug.zip.
details.commands_configs:
// Diagnostic ADB Commands for Android Enterprise
$ adb shell dumpsys device_policy > policy_dump.txt
$ adb logcat -v time -s DPM:V DevicePolicyManager:V clouddpc:V
$ adb shell dumpsys wifi | grep -E "SSID|mNetworkCapabilities|SupplicantState"
$ adb bugreport my_device_bugreport.zip
key_takeaways: Dumpsys device_policy contains the definitive truth of active restrictions, device owners, and delegated scopes.
Bugreports contain kernel dmesg, system logcat, memory dumps, and battery telemetry.
Certificate installation failures are commonly caused by missing intermediate CAs in the PKCS#12 payload.

quiz.question: Which ADB command provides the active restrictions and policies applied by the Device Policy Controller?
quiz.explanation: `adb shell dumpsys device_policy` outputs the active Device Owner, Profile Owner, delegated management scopes, password quality requirements, and applied policy restrictions.

quiz.question: When diagnosing a Wi-Fi 802.1X EAP-TLS certificate failure in Android logcat, which tag should you filter for?
quiz.explanation: `wpa_supplicant` is the core Linux/Android daemon responsible for WPA/WPA2/WPA3 enterprise Wi-Fi handshakes and certificate authentication validation.

quiz.question: Which tool can be used to visualize and analyze Android bugreport battery telemetry and app wake-locks?
quiz.explanation: Google Battery Historian parses Android bugreport.zip files into timeline charts showing screen on/off events, Wi-Fi wake-locks, and battery discharge rates.

workspace-one.name: Workspace ONE Essentials
workspace-one.description: Design and configure VMware Workspace ONE UEM console structures, smart groups, tunnel integrations, and enterprise app catalogs.

lessons.name: Module 1: Architecture & Console Setup
lessons.summary: Organizational group hierarchy, role-based access control, directory service sync, and cloud connector setup.

details.overview: Workspace ONE UEM (formerly AirWatch) uses an Organization Group (OG) hierarchy modeled after an enterprise corporate tree. Settings and profiles inherit from parent OGs down to child OGs, allowing regional delegation and granular policy scoping.
topics: Multi-tenant Organization Group (OG) design: Global, Customer, Regional, Division
Inherit vs Override settings mechanics
AirWatch Cloud Connector (ACC) for Active Directory / LDAP and Certificate Authority sync
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and custom administrator permission sets
lab_guide: Step 1: Log in to Workspace ONE UEM console and navigate to Groups & Settings > Organization Groups.
Step 2: Create a child OG named "Europe - Mobile Logistics" underneath the Customer OG.
Step 3: Change settings from "Inherit" to "Override" to enable customized regional branding.
Step 4: Verify directory integration test connectivity through the Cloud Connector.
details.commands_configs:
// Workspace ONE REST API Sample - Fetch Organization Group Details
GET /API/system/groups/1092
Host: as901.awmdm.com
aw-tenant-code: API_KEY_CORP_9918
Authorization: Basic YWRtaW5AdWVtbGFiczpjb25zb2xlMTIzIQ==
Accept: application/json
key_takeaways: Always assign devices and policies at the Customer OG level or below; never at Global.
AirWatch Cloud Connector initiates outbound HTTPS connections on port 443, eliminating the need for inbound firewall holes.
Settings inheritance saves administrative overhead when managing global baselines.

quiz.question: At which Organization Group level should enterprise devices and user profiles typically be configured?
options: Customer OG or its regional Child OGs
quiz.explanation: Devices and profiles must reside at the Customer OG level or beneath. The Global OG is strictly reserved for system architecture and hosting multi-tenant configurations.

quiz.question: Which network port does AirWatch Cloud Connector (ACC) require for outbound communication to the Workspace ONE UEM cloud console?
quiz.explanation: AirWatch Cloud Connector initiates only outbound HTTPS connections over TCP port 443 to Workspace ONE cloud, eliminating the need for incoming firewall holes.

quiz.question: What is the architectural effect of changing an Organization Group setting from "Inherit" to "Override"?
options: It deletes all enrolled devices in the child group
It breaks inheritance for that category, allowing the child OG to configure custom policies and branding independently
It blocks users from logging into the Self-Service Portal
It resets administrator passwords across the entire tenant
quiz.explanation: Selecting Override breaks inheritance for that specific settings category, allowing administrators of the child OG to apply tailored configurations.

lessons.name: Module 2: Device Profiling & Smart Groups
lessons.summary: Dynamic smart group assignment, multi-platform profile delivery, passcode policies, and compliance actions.

details.overview: Smart Groups are dynamic criteria-based targeting engines in Workspace ONE. Unlike static groups, Smart Groups evaluate endpoint attributes in real time, such as OS version, device model, ownership type, user department, or management status, ensuring profiles land only on appropriate endpoints.
topics: Constructing dynamic Smart Groups using boolean logic and device attributes
Profile payloads: Passcode, Wi-Fi 802.1x, VPN, Restrictions, Credentials
Exclusions and priority handling when profiles conflict
Automated compliance triggers: Jailbroken/Rooted detection, encryption enforcement
lab_guide: Step 1: Create a Smart Group named "Corporate Executives - iOS 17+".
Step 2: Add criteria: Ownership = Corporate Dedicated, Platform = Apple iOS, Minimum OS = 17.0.
Step 3: Create an iOS Profile containing an enterprise Wi-Fi certificate and Exchange ActiveSync payload.
Step 4: Assign the profile to the Smart Group and verify push status in the device event log.
key_takeaways: Smart Groups update membership automatically as devices enroll, upgrade OS, or change user assignments.
Exclusions take precedence over inclusions in Smart Group assignment.
Compliance policies can automatically strip profiles if an endpoint violates corporate rules.

quiz.question: How do Smart Groups in Workspace ONE differ from traditional static user groups?
options: Smart Groups require manual addition of every serial number
Smart Groups dynamically calculate membership based on live device attributes like OS version, model, and ownership
Smart Groups can only be used on Windows laptops
Smart Groups cost extra licensing per device
quiz.explanation: Smart Groups evaluate dynamic criteria (model, platform, ownership, OS build) and automatically add or remove endpoints as their status changes.

quiz.question: When both inclusions and exclusions are configured in a Workspace ONE Smart Group assignment, which rule takes precedence?
options: Whichever rule was configured most recently
The device operating system determines priority
quiz.explanation: In Workspace ONE UEM, exclusions always take precedence over inclusions to guarantee that restricted or testing populations are not inadvertently impacted.

quiz.question: Which push notification service is utilized by Workspace ONE to deliver profiles and MDM commands to iOS/iPadOS endpoints?
quiz.explanation: Apple mobile device management relies on APNs to wake up the device, prompting it to check in with the Workspace ONE MDM server over an encrypted TLS connection.

lessons.name: Module 3: Enterprise App Catalog & Tunnel
lessons.summary: Internal enterprise app packaging, per-app VPN with Workspace ONE Tunnel, and proxy gateways.

details.overview: Workspace ONE Tunnel provides micro-VPN per-app segmentation, routing confidential corporate intranet traffic securely back to internal data centers without tunneling personal browser or streaming traffic.
topics: Deploying the Unified Access Gateway (UAG) appliance for Tunnel routing
Per-App VPN configuration vs Device-Wide VPN
Device Traffic Rules (DTR) and split tunneling domains
App wrapping and Workspace ONE SDK integration for secure offline caching
lab_guide: Step 1: Deploy a Unified Access Gateway (UAG) virtual appliance with the Tunnel edge service enabled.
Step 2: In the UEM console, define Device Traffic Rules: Direct all "*.internal.uemlabs.com" traffic through the Tunnel gateway.
Step 3: Assign the Tunnel profile to the corporate Salesforce and intranet browser apps.
Step 4: Verify on the device that opening the internal URL establishes an on-demand VPN icon in the status bar.
details.commands_configs:
// Workspace ONE Tunnel Device Traffic Rules (DTR)
Rule 1:
  Name: "Intranet Core"
  App: "com.android.chrome"
  Destination: "*.corp.uemlabs.com:443"
  Action: "TUNNEL"
  TunnelGateway: "uag-edge.uemlabs.com:8443"

Rule 2:
  Name: "All Other Traffic"
  App: "ALL"
  Destination: "*"
  Action: "BYPASS"
key_takeaways: Per-app VPN safeguards corporate networks because unapproved apps cannot traverse the corporate tunnel.
Device Traffic Rules support domain wildcards, IP CIDR ranges, and port specifications.
Workspace ONE Tunnel requires client certificates for seamless passwordless authentication.

quiz.question: What is the primary security advantage of Per-App VPN over traditional full-device VPN?
options: It speeds up device battery charging
Only approved enterprise apps can access the corporate network; personal apps are prevented from touching internal servers
It eliminates the need for an internet connection
It turns on the device camera
quiz.explanation: Per-App VPN isolates network transmission so only designated corporate apps can tunnel into the internal corporate data center, isolating unmanaged personal traffic.

quiz.question: How does VMware Workspace ONE Tunnel provide secure intranet connectivity for enterprise applications?
options: By establishing a full-device layer 3 VPN that routes all personal traffic through the company datacenter
By providing per-app micro-segmentation that only routes authorized corporate app traffic through the Tunnel gateway
By publishing all internal servers to the public internet
quiz.explanation: Workspace ONE Tunnel utilizes Per-App VPN tunneling, routing only managed corporate application traffic to enterprise resources while leaving personal traffic completely untouched.

quiz.question: What format is used to push customized application configurations directly into managed mobile apps from the Workspace ONE console?
options: AppConfig XML / Managed Configurations key-value pairs
quiz.explanation: The AppConfig standard allows administrators to define key-value configuration dictionaries in the console that are injected directly into compliant enterprise applications upon install.

lessons.name: Module 4: Access Integration & SSO
lessons.summary: Workspace ONE Access SAML 2.0 federation, conditional access, and passwordless authentication with Mobile SSO.

details.overview: Workspace ONE Access functions as the identity provider (IdP) and conditional access engine, providing single sign-on across SaaS, web, and native mobile apps using SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect, and Mobile SSO certificate authentication.
topics: Configuring SAML 2.0 federation between Workspace ONE Access and Azure AD / Okta
Mobile SSO for Android (Cert-based authentication) and iOS (Kerberos / Cert)
Risk analytics and device posture verification before granting app access
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) step-up challenges based on network IP range
lab_guide: Step 1: In Workspace ONE Access, set up an Identity Provider linking to the UEM internal CA.
Step 2: Create an Access Policy: When authenticating from an enrolled managed device, accept Mobile SSO (cert).
Step 3: If device is unmanaged, require password + push notification MFA.
Step 4: Test single sign-on on an enrolled device opening the corporate Workday app.
details.commands_configs:
// SAML 2.0 Identity Assertion Attributes
<saml:Attribute Name="mail">
  <saml:AttributeValue>candidate@uemlabs.com</saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
<saml:Attribute Name="deviceUdid">
  <saml:AttributeValue>e8492048fbc09124</saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
<saml:Attribute Name="complianceStatus">
  <saml:AttributeValue>Compliant</saml:AttributeValue>
</saml:Attribute>
key_takeaways: Mobile SSO eliminates user password prompts by leveraging on-device user certificates.
Conditional Access evaluates device enrollment state and compliance before issuing an access token.
SAML assertions can pass custom device tags to cloud applications.

quiz.question: How does Mobile SSO in Workspace ONE achieve passwordless authentication?
options: By storing user passwords in plain text in browser cache
By using a secure cryptographic client certificate provisioned onto the enrolled device by the EMM
By dialing the user desk phone
quiz.explanation: Mobile SSO provisions an identity certificate to the device during enrollment; when accessing enterprise apps, the certificate performs mutual TLS authentication without passwords.

quiz.question: Which component enables Kerberos-based Mobile Single Sign-On (Mobile SSO) for managed iOS devices in Workspace ONE Access?
options: Built-in Kerberos Key Distribution Center (KDC) combined with device identity certificates
quiz.explanation: Mobile SSO for iOS uses a cloud/on-premises Kerberos KDC adapter that validates the device certificate pushed by Workspace ONE UEM, generating a Kerberos ticket without prompting the user.

quiz.question: What authentication standard is primarily used by Workspace ONE Access to federate identities to SaaS providers like Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and Workday?
quiz.explanation: Workspace ONE Access acts as an Identity Provider (IdP) utilizing modern SAML 2.0 and OIDC federation standards for seamless web and cloud application Single Sign-On.

lessons.name: Module 5: Intelligence & Automated Remediation
lessons.summary: Sensor telemetry, digital employee experience score, automated notification bots, and security posture rules.

details.overview: Workspace ONE Intelligence aggregates big data across endpoints, apps, and networks to deliver actionable insights, digital employee experience (DEX) metrics, and automated remediation workflows.
topics: Creating custom Windows and macOS sensors (PowerShell, Bash, Python)
Automated remediation workflows: If battery health < 60%, trigger ServiceNow ticket
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) tracking and OS patch telemetry
Freestyle Orchestrator multi-step workflow pipelines
lab_guide: Step 1: Write a PowerShell sensor that detects whether BitLocker encryption is enabled with a TPM chip.
Step 2: Build an Intelligence Automation: When sensor BitLocker == False, trigger high-priority alert and apply quarantine tag.
Step 3: Test sensor evaluation on a staged Windows 11 endpoint.
Step 4: Review telemetry dashboard.
key_takeaways: Sensors allow IT to query any hardware or registry parameter not natively exposed in the GUI.
Automations can interface with external systems like ServiceNow, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.
Freestyle Orchestrator chains software installs, scripts, and profiles conditionally.

quiz.question: What is the role of Sensors in Workspace ONE UEM?
options: They measure the ambient room temperature
They run custom PowerShell or Bash scripts on endpoints to report specific system, registry, or hardware telemetry back to the console
They detect smoke in the server room
They turn off the monitor when someone walks away
quiz.explanation: Sensors execute custom PowerShell, Bash, or Python scripts on managed devices to extract targeted hardware or software parameters and report them back to the EMM.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of Workspace ONE Intelligence automated Freestyle Orchestrator workflows?
options: Creating multi-step cross-platform automation that links sensors, scripts, app installs, and remediation actions based on real-time device conditions
Manually formatting hard drives on schedule
Sending mass marketing emails to candidates
quiz.explanation: Freestyle Orchestrator provides low-code conditional sequencing allowing admins to evaluate device states (Sensors) and conditionally run scripts or deploy software.

quiz.question: How does Workspace ONE Intelligence gather endpoint vulnerability telemetry across managed Windows and macOS fleets?
options: By correlating OS build numbers and patch levels against the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) CVE catalog
By performing active port scans against employee home routers
quiz.explanation: Workspace ONE Intelligence correlates endpoint inventory data with CVE vulnerability feeds to calculate risk scores and highlight unpatched vulnerabilities.

lessons.name: Module 6: Windows & macOS Endpoint Management
lessons.summary: Modern PC management via CSPs, Windows Update for Business, macOS configuration profiles, and FileVault encryption.

details.overview: Modern Management replaces legacy on-premises Group Policy Objects (GPOs) and imaging with over-the-air MDM Configuration Service Providers (CSPs), Apple APNs protocols, Windows Autopilot, and Apple Business Manager.
topics: Transitioning from domain-joined GPOs to cloud MDM CSPs
Windows Autopilot out-of-box provisioning
macOS automated enrollment via Apple Business Manager (ABM)
Managing FileVault encryption keys and escrowing Recovery Keys in the console
lab_guide: Step 1: Configure a Windows Update for Business profile establishing a 7-day Quality update deferral ring.
Step 2: Create a BitLocker profile requiring 256-bit XTS-AES encryption and TPM 2.0 protector.
Step 3: Deploy an enterprise Win32 application packaged as an .intunewin or .zip payload with silent install switches.
Step 4: Verify escrowed recovery keys in the UEM console Security tab.
key_takeaways: Modern PC management allows remote laptops to receive security patches anywhere without connecting to corporate VPN.
BitLocker and FileVault keys must be escrowed in the EMM to prevent unrecoverable data loss.
Apple MDM uses the Apple Push Notification service (APNs) as the signaling mechanism.

quiz.question: Why is modern cloud PC management favored over legacy Active Directory GPOs for hybrid workers?
options: Because modern cloud management updates policies and patches over any internet connection without requiring a line-of-sight VPN to an on-prem domain controller
Because modern management deletes the operating system weekly
Because GPOs only work on mobile phones
Because cloud management eliminates the need for software licenses
quiz.explanation: Modern PC management utilizes cloud MDM channels, enabling remote laptops to receive security baselines, updates, and software over any public Wi-Fi without needing an on-prem domain connection.

quiz.question: Which native Windows enrollment method allows zero-touch provisioning of brand new corporate PCs directly from the OEM box?
options: Windows Autopilot combined with Workspace ONE modern management
Legacy Ghost imaging over PXE boot
quiz.explanation: Windows Autopilot integrates hardware hashes with Entra ID and Workspace ONE to automatically configure, encrypt, and provision Windows 10/11 laptops straight out of the OEM shipping box.

quiz.question: On macOS, which mechanism does Apple mandate for managing system extensions, kernel extensions, and security settings?
options: Apple MDM configuration profiles signed with enterprise certificates
Disabling System Integrity Protection (SIP) via terminal
quiz.explanation: Apple strictly requires MDM configuration profiles for managing privacy preferences (PPPC), system extensions, and FileVault encryption on modern macOS versions.

soti-mobicontrol.name: SOTI MobiControl Mastery
soti-mobicontrol.description: End-to-end administration of SOTI MobiControl: deployment servers, device add rules, custom scripting engine, and lockdown kiosk profiles.

lessons.name: Module 1: Architecture, Deployment Servers & Agents
lessons.summary: Deployment Server setup, Management Service, database sizing, and agent generation for varied OS builds.

details.overview: SOTI MobiControl is a market leader for rugged, frontline, and industrial mobile computing. Its architecture consists of the Management Service, Deployment Server (DS), MS SQL Database, and on-device MobiControl Agents communicating over persistent TCP/WebSocket connections.
topics: MobiControl architecture: Management Server vs Deployment Server (DS)
Generating customized Android, Zebra, and Windows CE/Embedded agents
SOTI Cloud Link for on-premises resource bridging
Deployment Server load balancing and high-availability sizing
lab_guide: Step 1: Open the MobiControl Administration Utility (MCAU) and verify Deployment Server status.
Step 2: Generate a custom Android Enterprise agent bound to your production server URL.
Step 3: Staging via MobiControl enrollment barcode on a Zebra TC57.
Step 4: Verify agent connectivity and status in the web console.
details.commands_configs:
// Agent Enrollment Parameter String
serverurl=https://ds01.uemlabs.com:443;enrollmentid=UEM_CORP_LOGISTICS;user=svc_enroll;devicename=%IMEI%
key_takeaways: The Deployment Server manages direct communication with devices; multiple DS nodes can be clustered.
Agent generation allows embedding enrollment credentials for one-scan provisioning.
MobiControl supports Android, iOS, Windows, Linux, and legacy Windows Mobile/CE.

quiz.question: Which component in SOTI MobiControl directly handles real-time socket connections to enrolled devices?
quiz.explanation: The Deployment Server (DS) is the core high-performance engine that maintains real-time TCP/WebSocket sockets with devices for instant command execution.

quiz.question: Which server component in SOTI MobiControl handles real-time device check-in, script execution, and policy delivery?
quiz.explanation: The Deployment Server (DS) is the core engine that maintains persistent TCP connections with endpoint agents, executing scripts and streaming device data.

quiz.question: What protocol and default port does the SOTI MobiControl device agent use to connect securely to the Deployment Server?
quiz.explanation: SOTI MobiControl agents communicate with Deployment Servers over port 5494 (or 443 in modern HTTPS setups) protected by mutual TLS certificates.

lessons.name: Module 2: Rule Configuration & Device Add Rules
lessons.summary: Device Connection Rules, enrollment enrollment IDs, automated device naming, and folder grouping logic.

details.overview: Device Add Rules define how new devices enter the MobiControl system. Through Enrollment IDs, rules determine the destination device group folder, naming conventions using macros (e.g., %MAC%, %SERIAL%, %IMEI%), authentication requirements, and initial profile bindings.
topics: Configuring Device Add Rules for Android Enterprise, iOS, and Windows
Device naming macros and automated prefixing (e.g. WH04-TC52-%SERIAL%)
Auto-grouping devices based on IP subnets, carrier APNs, or enrollment credentials
File Sync Rules and Device Relocation Rules
lab_guide: Step 1: In the MobiControl console, navigate to the Rules tab > Add Rule > Device Add Rule.
Step 2: Select Android Enterprise > Managed Google Play.
Step 3: Configure Device Naming formula: "ZBR-%MODEL%-%MAC:6%".
Step 4: Set the Target Folder to "Corporate Logistics / Chicago Distribution Center".
details.commands_configs:
// Device Naming Macro Pattern Examples
Prefix: WH01-
Macro 1: %MODEL%
Macro 2: -
Macro 3: %SERIAL%
Result: WH01-TC52-20188402
key_takeaways: Enrollment IDs allow frontline workers to provision devices with a short code without entering passwords.
Relocation rules automatically move devices between folders if their Wi-Fi BSSID or IP changes.
Consistent device naming prevents inventory duplicates in large enterprise fleets.

quiz.question: What macro in SOTI MobiControl device naming resolves to the device hardware serial number?
quiz.explanation: %SERIAL% dynamically queries the hardware manufacturer serial number from the kernel and embeds it into the device display name.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of an Enrollment URL or Enrollment ID in a SOTI Device Add Rule?
options: It routes the enrolling device to the correct Deployment Server and assigns it to a target device group automatically
It formats the device SD card
It changes the device cellular carrier
It purchases Play Store gift cards
quiz.explanation: An Enrollment ID maps the endpoint to a specific Device Add Rule, defining authentication requirements, target device groups, and initial profile baselines.

quiz.question: How can an administrator enforce user authentication during SOTI enrollment?
options: By integrating Active Directory / Azure AD (Entra ID) into the Device Add Rule credentials requirement
By asking users to mail their employee badge to IT
By requiring a captcha on every reboot
By setting a static pin for the entire company
quiz.explanation: SOTI Device Add Rules can be linked to LDAP/AD or Entra ID so users must enter corporate credentials before the device registers.

lessons.name: Module 3: Package Studio & Scripting Engine
lessons.summary: Build .pcg deployment packages, pre/post installation scripts, writefile commands, and intent broadcasts.

details.overview: SOTI Package Studio allows engineers to package apps, configurations, drivers, and files into compressed `.pcg` deployment bundles. SOTI’s built-in script engine supports deep device manipulation using legacy syntax and modern JavaScript scripts.
topics: Creating multi-file packages in SOTI Package Studio (.pcg)
Pre-install and Post-install execution scripts
SOTI Script commands: `writeprivateprofstring`, `sendintent`, `install`, `del`
JavaScript engine in MobiControl for advanced conditional device logic
lab_guide: Step 1: Open SOTI Package Studio and add an APK plus a custom configuration file "config.json".
Step 2: Write a post-install script: writeprivateprofstring to configure internal flags.
Step 3: Build the .pcg package and upload it to the MobiControl Package Library.
Step 4: Assign the package to a test device profile and verify deployment.
key_takeaways: Packages can contain pre-scripts to terminate running processes before applying an update.
SOTI scripts execute with root or device-owner system privileges on supported OEM hardware.
JavaScript scripting in MobiControl v15+ allows HTTP REST calls directly from on-device scripts.

quiz.question: Which SOTI script command sends a standard Android Intent broadcast to an installed application?
quiz.explanation: `sendintent` is the native SOTI script command used to dispatch explicit and implicit Android Intents, pass extra flags, and wake up background receivers.

quiz.question: Which SOTI script command is used to silently install an Android APK package located in the device temporary storage?
quiz.explanation: SOTI scripting engine uses `install` (or `install -installflags` on Android+) to programmatically deploy and upgrade application packages silently.

quiz.question: What utility in SOTI MobiControl packages applications, scripts, and pre-requisite files into a deployable .pcg package?
quiz.explanation: SOTI Package Studio builds .pcg packages containing payload files along with pre-install and post-install automation scripts.

lessons.name: Module 4: Remote Control & Diagnostic Tools
lessons.summary: Real-time HTML5 remote screen capture, file explorer transfer, terminal execution, and device event logs.

details.overview: MobiControl features a comprehensive Remote Control suite that allows helpdesk technicians to view and control endpoints in real time, browse the remote filesystem, pull diagnostic logs, and terminate processes without interrupting the user.
topics: HTML5 Web Remote Control vs Java Remote Control Plugin
Remote File Explorer: Uploading, downloading, and editing files on the fly
Remote Task Manager: Inspecting CPU, memory, and terminating frozen tasks
Command-line console execution on remote endpoints
lab_guide: Step 1: Locate an active device in the MobiControl console and click "Remote Control".
Step 2: Use the keyboard shortcuts to simulate Android hardware buttons (Home, Back, Recent Apps).
Step 3: Open the Remote File Explorer and retrieve the application log file from /sdcard/Download/.
Step 4: Send a remote script command to flush DNS cache.
details.commands_configs:
// Remote Terminal Quick Commands
$ netstat -an
$ getprop ro.build.version.release
$ ping -c 4 gateway.uemlabs.com
key_takeaways: Remote control on rugged devices (Zebra, Honeywell) requires no user acceptance prompt if configured in policy.
File explorer transfers bypass the need to connect endpoints via physical USB cables.
Session recording can be mandated for compliance and auditing.

quiz.question: Can helpdesk administrators transfer files directly to and from a remote Android device using SOTI Remote Control without a physical USB cable?
options: Yes, using the integrated Remote File Explorer over the active network connection
No, files can only be transferred with an SD card adapter
quiz.explanation: The Remote File Explorer in SOTI Remote Control allows bidirectional file transfers, renaming, and permission edits over cellular or Wi-Fi.

quiz.question: What is the key advantage of SOTI Assist when troubleshooting frontline warehouse devices?
options: It provides remote screen sharing, file transfer, process inspection, and integrated ticketing directly from the MobiControl console
quiz.explanation: SOTI Assist is an integrated remote support and diagnostics solution providing live screen control, event logs, file syncing, and ticket management for frontline fleets.

quiz.question: How can a technician inspect background processes and kill a frozen application on a remote Android scanner via SOTI?
options: Using the SOTI Remote Control Task Manager tab or sending the kill_process script command
By power cycling the entire facility
By waiting for the battery to drain completely
quiz.explanation: SOTI remote control includes a Task Manager tab showing live CPU/RAM usage per process, allowing technicians to kill or inspect hung processes remotely.

lessons.name: Module 5: Lockdown / Kiosk Mode & Profiles
lessons.summary: Interactive kiosk template creation, single-app and multi-app lockdowns, status bar hiding, and auth pins.

details.overview: MobiControl Lockdown replaces the standard Android home screen with a secure, branded kiosk shell. Users can only launch authorized corporate apps, preventing access to the device settings, YouTube, browser, or unapproved features.
topics: Single-app lockdown (Kiosk) vs Multi-app launcher
HTML5 template design with custom corporate logos and status indicators (Wi-Fi, Battery)
Disabling notification pulldowns, status bars, and USB debugging
Administrator bypass passwords to unlock standard launcher in the field
lab_guide: Step 1: In Profiles, select Android Enterprise > Configuration > Lockdown.
Step 2: Add two applications: "Inventory Scanner" and "Package Dispatch".
Step 3: Check "Disable System Status Bar" and set an Admin Bypass Password.
Step 4: Apply profile to test device and confirm the standard Android launcher is blocked.
details.commands_configs:
// HTML Template Variable Macros for Custom SOTI Lockdown
Device: %SERIAL% IP: %IP% Battery: %
Warehouse App Support Chat
key_takeaways: Lockdown prevents workers from tampering with device settings or installing games.
Custom HTML/CSS templates allow companies to create branded corporate interfaces.
Admin bypass credentials allow on-site supervisors to troubleshoot without revoking the profile.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of the SOTI MobiControl Lockdown profile?
options: To restrict user access strictly to authorized enterprise applications and block access to unapproved settings and apps
To encrypt the device hard drive with BitLocker
To set the device wallpaper to a random photo
To turn off the Wi-Fi card permanently
quiz.explanation: Lockdown replaces the standard Android launcher with a secure kiosk shell that strictly limits user interaction to approved enterprise applications.

quiz.question: How does SOTI MobiControl generate customized kiosk home screens for rugged shift workers?
options: By rendering an HTML/CSS lockdown template that restricts access strictly to allowed app shortcuts and system settings
By physically soldering buttons on the motherboard
By deleting the Android operating system
By turning off the screen backlight
quiz.explanation: SOTI Lockdown mode replaces the system launcher with an HTML template presenting only approved icons, preventing users from tampering with settings or games.

quiz.question: What keyboard shortcut or gesture allows a field supervisor to temporarily exit SOTI Lockdown mode and access native Android settings?
options: An administrator password bypass configured in the Lockdown Profile
quiz.explanation: Administrators can set an Admin Exit Password in the Lockdown profile so technicians can access native settings on-site without unenrolling the device.

lessons.name: Module 6: Zebra StageNow Integration & OTA
lessons.summary: Generate StageNow barcodes with MobiControl enrollment payload, OS firmware updates, and rapid unbox staging.

details.overview: Zebra StageNow is the industry standard for staging Zebra mobile computers. By combining StageNow XML profiles with SOTI MobiControl, administrators can stage an entire warehouse fleet in minutes by scanning a single 2D barcode.
topics: Zebra StageNow Workstation architecture and MX (Mobility Extensions)
Generating 2D StageNow barcodes with Wi-Fi, NTP, and SOTI Agent payloads
Over-the-Air (OTA) OS firmware updates using Zebra LifeGuard
Battery lifecycle and touch screen sensitivity profiles (glove mode, rain mode)
lab_guide: Step 1: Open Zebra StageNow Workstation and create a "Connect Wi-Fi & Enroll in MDM" profile.
Step 2: Embed the enterprise staging WPA2-Enterprise credentials and MobiControl APK download URL.
Step 3: Generate a PDF staging sheet with the 2D Aztec/DataMatrix barcode.
Step 4: Unbox a brand-new Zebra scanner, scan the barcode, and observe automated staging.
details.commands_configs:
// Zebra StageNow MX XML Payload Snippet
<wap-provisioningdoc>
  <characteristic type="Profile">
    <parm name="ProfileName" value="SotiEnrollment"/>
    <characteristic type="Wi-Fi">
      <parm name="SSID" value="CorpWarehouse"/>
      <parm name="SecurityMode" value="WPA2-PSK"/>
      <parm name="PreSharedKey" value="ZbrSecureStaging99!"/>
    </characteristic>
    <characteristic type="AppMgr">
      <parm name="Action" value="Install"/>
      <parm name="APK" value="https://ds.uemlabs.com/agents/mobicontrol.apk"/>
    </characteristic>
  </characteristic>
</wap-provisioningdoc>
key_takeaways: StageNow barcodes allow staging without typing Wi-Fi passwords or enrollment URLs.
Zebra LifeGuard OTA updates can be scheduled through MobiControl to prevent shift downtime.
MX allows configuring hardware scanner engines, touch modes, and physical audio volumes.

quiz.question: How do warehouse technicians typically stage a new Zebra rugged handheld using StageNow?
options: By scanning a 2D configuration barcode printed on a paper sheet or displayed on a monitor
By typing 40-character URLs manually using on-screen keyboard
By calling customer service on the telephone
quiz.explanation: Technicians simply power on the device and scan the StageNow 2D barcode, which instantly programs Wi-Fi, clock, certificates, and initiates MDM enrollment.

quiz.question: How does SOTI MobiControl integrate with Zebra StageNow for rapid device staging?
options: By scanning a StageNow 2D barcode that automatically connects to Wi-Fi, downloads the SOTI agent, and executes the Enrollment ID
By typing 100 lines of code manually on each scanner
By connecting each device to a desktop computer via serial cable
By Bluetooth pairing with a microwave
quiz.explanation: Zebra StageNow encodes Wi-Fi credentials and agent download instructions into barcodes or NFC tags for one-scan automated enrollment into SOTI.

quiz.question: Which Zebra firmware subsystem does SOTI configure when deploying OEMConfig or MX XML profiles?
quiz.explanation: Zebra MX (Mobility Extensions) provides an enterprise-ready software layer on Zebra Android devices that exposes hardware settings to EMMs like SOTI.

ivanti-neurons.name: Ivanti Neurons for UEM
ivanti-neurons.description: Autonomous endpoint discovery, real-time edge intelligence sensors, machine learning vulnerability remediation, and MobileIron cloud migration.

lessons.name: Module 1: Neurons Discovery & Asset Inventory
lessons.summary: Active and passive network discovery, asset reconciliation, agentless sensor queries, and normalized hardware inventory.

details.overview: Ivanti Neurons for Discovery provides 360-degree visibility across the IT estate. Combining active network scanning, passive listening, and agentless connectors, it discovers unknown shadow IT endpoints and reconciles them into an actionable inventory.
topics: Active subnet discovery vs passive network eavesdropping
Reconciling duplicate assets across Active Directory, Azure AD, SCCM, and Intune
Normalizing software titles and identifying unused software licenses
Edge agent deployment for continuous telemetry collection
lab_guide: Step 1: Configure a Discovery Connector linked to your enterprise virtualization cluster.
Step 2: Run a subnet discovery sweep on 10.200.0.0/24.
Step 3: Review the Asset Reconciliation dashboard to merge duplicate entries.
Step 4: Tag newly discovered unmanaged devices for automated onboarding.
key_takeaways: Asset reconciliation prevents duplicate licensing costs by merging multiple agent records for the same device.
Passive discovery alerts IT the instant an unauthorized rogue device connects to corporate Ethernet.
Normalizing software titles simplifies vendor audit compliance.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of asset reconciliation in Ivanti Neurons?
options: It merges multiple discovery records for the same physical computer into one single accurate asset view
It permanently erases all log files
It creates multiple fake computer names
quiz.explanation: Asset reconciliation uses machine learning to match serial numbers, MAC addresses, and hostnames across disparate data sources, merging duplicates into one unified record.

quiz.question: How does Ivanti Neurons active and passive discovery identify unmanaged devices on a corporate subnet?
options: By listening to ARP requests, network broadcasts, and running authenticated WMI/SSH probes to discover rogue endpoints
By asking employees to report their colleagues
quiz.explanation: Ivanti Neurons combines passive listening (ARP/DHCP sniffing) and active subnet scanning to discover unmanaged devices and shadow IT before they access corporate resources.

quiz.question: What lightweight agent component is deployed to endpoints to stream hardware, software, and health telemetry to Ivanti Neurons?
quiz.explanation: The Ivanti Neurons Agent provides endpoint discovery, self-healing automation, and patch compliance telemetry with minimal CPU overhead.

lessons.name: Module 2: Automated Remediation Bots
lessons.summary: Deploy pre-packaged and custom Neurons bots to detect and self-heal disk latency, crashed services, and corrupted agents.

details.overview: Neurons Bots provide autonomous self-healing for endpoints. By running background diagnostics, bots detect issues (e.g., failed antivirus service, impending disk failure, corrupt registry keys) and automatically resolve them before the user notices a problem.
topics: Neurons Bot triggers: Scheduled, Telemetry threshold, and Event-based
Pre-packaged self-healing bots: Spooler restart, Disk cleanup, Certificate renewal
Building custom bot logic flows with branching conditional decisions
Interactive vs silent bot execution
lab_guide: Step 1: In the Neurons console, navigate to Automation > Bots > Create Bot.
Step 2: Set trigger: Daily at 06:00 AM on all Sales Department laptops.
Step 3: Add Action: Check status of "CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor" service.
Step 4: Add Remediation: If status == Stopped, attempt restart; if still failing, notify IT alert channel.
details.commands_configs:
// Sample Bot Flow Definition
Trigger:
  Condition: "Low Disk Space < 10%"
Action:
  - Step 1: Run System Cleanmgr temp file purge
  - Step 2: Empty Recycle Bin
  - Step 3: Re-evaluate Disk Space
  - Branch:
      If Disk Space > 15%: Send "Resolved" notification to log
      Else: Create ServiceNow Incident Priority 3
key_takeaways: Autonomous bots reduce helpdesk ticket volume by self-healing common recurring issues.
Bots run locally at the edge, executing even when endpoints are offline from the cloud.
Always test custom bots on a pilot group before broad enterprise rollout.

quiz.question: How do Ivanti Neurons Bots reduce helpdesk ticket volume?
options: By automatically detecting and self-healing common system faults (like crashed services or low disk space) before users submit tickets
By turning off the phone lines in the IT department
By preventing users from submitting questions
quiz.explanation: Neurons Bots autonomously detect and remediate endpoint issues in the background, eliminating the primary causes of level-1 helpdesk support tickets.

quiz.question: What are Neurons Bots in the Ivanti platform?
options: Autonomous self-healing automation routines that detect endpoint issues (e.g. hung services, low disk space, crashing apps) and resolve them without human intervention
quiz.explanation: Neurons Bots run diagnostic checks continuously and automatically execute remediation scripts when common IT issues or configuration drifts are detected.

quiz.question: Which metric measures the reduction in helpdesk tickets achieved by automated Neurons self-healing bots?
options: First-Contact Resolution (FCR) and Shift-Left MTTR (Mean Time to Resolution)
quiz.explanation: Self-healing bots shift resolution left to Tier 0, solving problems before employees notice them and reducing Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR).

lessons.name: Module 3: Patch Intelligence & Zero-Day Updates
lessons.summary: Risk-based vulnerability scoring, threat-aware patch testing, pilot rings, and automated endpoint patching schedules.

details.overview: Ivanti Neurons for Patch Intelligence shifts IT from reactive patch cycles to threat-aware vulnerability remediation. By correlating CVE data with active exploit intelligence, it prioritizes critical patches that protect against active ransomware and zero-day threats.
topics: VRR (Vulnerability Risk Rating) vs generic CVSS scores
Correlating patches with known active ransomware campaigns
Staged deployment rings: Canary, Pilot, Broad, and Critical Server groups
Automated rollback triggers if patch reliability threshold drops
lab_guide: Step 1: Open the Patch Intelligence dashboard and filter for "Actively Weaponized Vulnerabilities".
Step 2: Create a Patch Group for third-party applications (Chrome, Zoom, Adobe Acrobat).
Step 3: Schedule a Pilot Ring rollout to 5% of devices with a 48-hour soak window.
Step 4: Monitor installation success rate and patch reboot prompts.
key_takeaways: Generic CVSS scores lack real-world context; weaponized threat intelligence identifies true operational risk.
Third-party application vulnerabilities represent over 70% of endpoint attack surfaces.
Configurable reboot countdowns prevent accidental data loss for active employees.

quiz.question: Why is threat-aware patch prioritization superior to simply patching everything by date?
options: It focuses immediate patching efforts on vulnerabilities that are actively weaponized and exploited by ransomware in the wild
It skips all Windows security updates
It lets users choose whether they want security or not
quiz.explanation: Threat-aware patch prioritization identifies vulnerabilities currently being exploited in live attacks, allowing IT to remediate high-risk vectors immediately.

quiz.question: How does Ivanti Patch Intelligence prioritize CVE vulnerabilities for enterprise patching?
options: By correlating CVSS severity scores with active threat actor exploitability and real-world weaponization telemetry
By patching whichever app was installed first
quiz.explanation: Ivanti Patch Intelligence uses machine learning and threat feeds to focus patching efforts on vulnerabilities that are actively being weaponized by adversaries in the wild.

quiz.question: In Ivanti Neurons Patch for Endpoints, what capability allows patching mobile remote workers who never connect to the office VPN?
options: Cloud-native patch distribution directly from global CDNs over HTTPS
Requiring all workers to fly to the corporate headquarters
Delivering USB thumb drives via postal mail
Printing patch binary code on paper
quiz.explanation: Ivanti Neurons delivers cloud-native patch content over HTTPS directly to endpoints wherever they are connected to the internet.

lessons.name: Module 4: MobileIron Cloud / Core Migration
lessons.summary: Tenant linking, policy transition from MobileIron Core to Neurons, certificate authority sync, and device re-homing.

details.overview: Following the acquisition of MobileIron, organizations with legacy MobileIron Core (on-prem) or MobileIron Cloud tenants must migrate to modern Ivanti Neurons for UEM. This lesson covers seamless tenant linking, policy mapping, and zero-touch device migration.
topics: Tenant linking architecture between MobileIron Core and Ivanti Neurons
Automated translation of MobileIron Labels to Neurons Device Groups
Over-the-Air device re-homing without requiring factory resets
Verifying PKI and Sentry Gateway traffic transitions
lab_guide: Step 1: Install the Neurons Connector on the MobileIron Core appliance.
Step 2: Sync device inventories, labels, and configurations into the Neurons cloud tenant.
Step 3: Execute a migration batch on a pilot department to repoint the agent management URL.
Step 4: Confirm endpoint check-in and certificate validation in the Neurons console.

# show sopt
# show mdm checkin-status
# ping neurons-cloud.ivanti.com
key_takeaways: Tenant linking allows administrators to manage legacy Core endpoints from the Neurons cloud console.
Seamless re-homing eliminates the need to recall devices or ask users to re-enroll.
Certificate authority continuity ensures Wi-Fi and VPN access remains uninterrupted.

quiz.question: What is the primary objective of tenant linking when migrating from MobileIron Core to Ivanti Neurons?
options: To manage existing on-prem endpoints from the modern cloud interface without forcing user re-enrollment
To convert all computers into mobile phones
quiz.explanation: Tenant linking connects the on-premise MobileIron Core database with the Neurons cloud platform, enabling centralized cloud management without disrupting enrolled devices.

quiz.question: When migrating legacy MobileIron Core (EPMM) tenants to Ivanti Neurons for UEM, how are device ownership and policies transitioned?
options: Through automated cloud migration bridges that map labels and configurations to modern Neurons policy sets with minimal user re-enrollment
By wiping every phone and firing all users
By buying new phones for every employee
quiz.explanation: Ivanti provides cloud migration tooling that transfers device records, labels, and configurations from on-premises MobileIron Core into cloud-hosted Neurons.

quiz.question: Which protocol does MobileIron / Ivanti use to secure corporate traffic from mobile devices to internal intranets?
options: MobileIron Sentry (AppConnect and Tunnel per-app VPN)
quiz.explanation: MobileIron Sentry provides secure reverse-proxy and per-app VPN tunneling for mobile devices accessing on-premises Exchange and web resources.

lessons.name: Module 5: Edge Intelligence & Machine Learning
lessons.summary: Natural language queries across thousands of edge endpoints in seconds, battery degradation alerts, and performance metrics.

details.overview: Edge Intelligence queries tens of thousands of endpoints in real time (within 1–3 seconds) using sub-second peer-to-peer and edge search algorithms. IT teams can ask natural-language questions to diagnose performance spikes, battery failures, and network latency.
topics: Sub-second query execution across distributed global endpoints
Natural Language Query (NLQ) engine: "Show laptops with battery health < 50%"
Real-time CPU and memory hog identification across user fleets
Benchmarking Digital Employee Experience (DEX) scores across business units
lab_guide: Step 1: In the Edge Intelligence console, enter query: "Processes with CPU usage > 80%".
Step 2: Identify rogue runaway processes across the fleet in real-time.
Step 3: Execute a remote kill command across affected endpoints.
Step 4: View the DEX trend graph after remediation.
key_takeaways: Edge Intelligence retrieves live device state without querying stale database records.
DEX scoring measures boots, app crashes, and latency to detect employee dissatisfaction early.
Immediate peer-to-peer data retrieval speeds up live incident response.

quiz.question: How fast can Ivanti Edge Intelligence return live system data from tens of thousands of endpoints?
quiz.explanation: Edge Intelligence queries endpoints in real time, gathering live sensor responses across tens of thousands of connected machines within seconds.

quiz.question: What is the primary query engine used by Ivanti Neurons Edge Intelligence to query live endpoints in under 10 seconds?
options: Real-time distributed edge processing querying RAM, disk, event logs, and network state across thousands of endpoints simultaneously
Running nightly batch SQL queries on an old tape drive
quiz.explanation: Edge Intelligence queries thousands of endpoints in seconds using distributed edge architecture, delivering real-time visibility into active processes and network connectivity.

quiz.question: How does Digital Employee Experience (DEX) scoring in Ivanti Neurons help IT organizations?
options: It quantifies device boot times, application crashes, and OS performance to proactively address employee friction before complaints occur
It monitors employee keystrokes for surveillance
quiz.explanation: DEX scoring provides visibility into application crashes, latency, and boot times so IT can proactively fix degradation before it harms productivity.

rugged-devices.name: Rugged & Frontline Devices
rugged-devices.description: Hardware configuration, barcode scanning SDKs, DataWedge intent APIs, StageNow XML profiles, shift-worker shared devices, and battery lifecycle.

lessons.name: Module 1: Zebra, Honeywell & Datalogic Hardware
lessons.summary: Rugged form factors, gun-grip ergonomics, drop-spec ratings, physical scanning heads, and cradle architecture.

details.overview: Rugged frontline mobile computers (Zebra TC5x/MC9300, Honeywell CT60/Dolphin, Datalogic Memor) operate under harsh conditions like sub-zero freezers, hazardous chemical plants, and heavy drop industrial warehouses. This module explores drop specifications (MIL-STD-810H), IP ratings, and cradle architectures.
topics: Form factors: Handheld touch computers vs pistol-grip gun devices vs vehicle-mounted terminals
Ingress Protection (IP65 vs IP67 vs IP68) and drop ratings (up to 10ft onto concrete)
Scan engines: 1D linear lasers, 2D imagers, and Extended Range (SE4850) reading up to 70ft
Multi-slot Ethernet and USB charging cradle infrastructure
lab_guide: Step 1: Inspect hardware specifications and temperature operational limits of Zebra MC9300.
Step 2: Configure scan engine targeting reticle (green dot vs red laser aiming crosshair).
Step 3: Setup multi-slot cradle network addressing in the warehouse comms room.
Step 4: Verify battery charging status indicators.
