Operating Temp: -20°C to 50°C (-4°F to 122°F)
key_takeaways: Extended-range imagers allow forklift operators to scan pallet barcodes from the vehicle without dismounting.
Cold storage (freezer) models feature heated scan windows to prevent condensation fogging.
Ethernet cradles provide high-speed automated OS flashing during overnight charging.

quiz.question: What special hardware feature is required on rugged handhelds operating in sub-zero freezer warehouses?
options: Condensation-resistant heated scan windows and low-temperature battery chemistry
Solar panels on the back cover
quiz.explanation: Freezer-rated mobile computers incorporate heated scan windows and internal heating elements to prevent rapid condensation and frost when transitioning between cold rooms and warm docks.

quiz.question: Why do enterprise warehouse operations deploy purpose-built rugged mobile computers rather than consumer smartphones?
options: Rugged devices feature drop ratings (MIL-STD-810H), IP67/68 sealing, dedicated physical barcode engines, and long-lifecycle enterprise OS support
Rugged devices are cheaper plastic toys
Consumer phones have larger batteries that last 5 days
Rugged devices do not use electricity
quiz.explanation: Rugged devices survive repeated drops onto concrete, operate in freezer environments (-30°C), and feature dedicated scan engines capable of reading barcodes from 50 feet away.

quiz.question: Which company develops the DataWedge scanning API framework used across enterprise mobile computers?
quiz.explanation: Zebra DataWedge is the enterprise API and service that interfaces with integrated barcode scan engines on Zebra Android devices.

lessons.name: Module 2: Barcode Scanning & DataWedge APIs
lessons.summary: DataWedge profile automation, keystroke output, broadcast intents, symbology configuration (UPC, QR, DataMatrix).

details.overview: Zebra DataWedge (and Honeywell Enterprise Wedge) intercepts optical barcode scans and translates them into either keystroke emulation or direct Android Broadcast Intents. This allows legacy and modern enterprise apps to receive barcode data without writing custom low-level camera drivers.
topics: DataWedge profiles: Associating specific profiles with target Android app package names
Keystroke output vs Intent output (best practice for reliability and speed)
Advanced Data Formatting (ADF): Stripping leading zeroes, appending Tabs or Enter keys
Symbology management: Enabling Code 128, DataMatrix, PDF417, GS1-128, and disabling unused formats
lab_guide: Step 1: On a Zebra device, open the DataWedge application.
Step 2: Create a new profile named "WarehouseAppProfile" and associate it with "com.uemlabs.inventory".
Step 3: Disable Keystroke Output and enable Intent Output with Action: "com.uemlabs.ACTION_BARCODE".
Step 4: In ADF (Advanced Data Formatting), configure a rule to append an Enter key [0x0D] after every scan.
key_takeaways: Intent output is far superior to Keystroke output because it eliminates cursor focus race conditions.
Disabling unused barcode symbologies improves scan engine decode speed and battery life.
Advanced Data Formatting (ADF) can reformat strings before passing them to the business application.

quiz.question: Why is Intent Output preferred over Keystroke Output in enterprise Android barcode scanning applications?
options: Because Intent Output passes the full scanned string directly to the application via an Android broadcast, regardless of whether a text input cursor is currently focused on screen
Because Keystroke Output requires an external mechanical typewriter
Because Intents make the barcode appear in color
Because Keystroke output only works on Apple iPhones
quiz.explanation: Intent Output reliably delivers scan data directly into the application logic, preventing lost characters or keystroke misdirection if the user accidentally taps outside an input box.

quiz.question: How does Zebra DataWedge transmit decoded barcode data to an enterprise web application or native Android app without code changes?
options: Keystroke output simulation (injecting decoded characters into the active input cursor)
By playing a sound through the speaker
By writing text to the lockscreen wallpaper
quiz.explanation: DataWedge Keystroke output simulates typing the scanned barcode characters directly into whatever field has cursor focus, allowing legacy web apps to work without SDK integration.

quiz.question: What Android mechanism does DataWedge use to broadcast barcode data asynchronously to native enterprise applications?
options: Android Intent broadcasts (with custom action and extras bundle containing symbology and raw data)
quiz.explanation: Intent output is the high-performance programmatic interface in DataWedge, delivering decoded barcode string and symbology type via Android Intent broadcasts.

lessons.name: Module 3: StageNow XML & Barcode Deployment
lessons.summary: StageNow Workstation tool, MX architecture, generating 2D barcodes for Wi-Fi, NTP, clock, and MDM agent enrollment.

details.overview: Zebra StageNow is the standard staging tool for Zebra Android devices. StageNow leverages Zebra Mobility Extensions (MX) to execute low-level configuration steps directly through barcode scans, NFC tags, or audio files.
topics: StageNow profile creation wizard: Wi-Fi, Network Clock, App Installation, MDM Staging
Generating 2D Aztec, DataMatrix, and PDF417 staging barcodes
Staging via USB / SD Card / NFC tap
Exporting XML for zero-touch mass deployment through EMM OEMConfig
lab_guide: Step 1: Open Zebra StageNow Workstation and create a new Xpert Mode profile.
Step 2: Add Wi-Fi configuration (WPA2-Enterprise with root CA certificate).
Step 3: Add FileMgr module to download the enterprise client APK from internal web server.
Step 4: Generate 2D barcode and test scan on a factory-reset Zebra device.
details.commands_configs:
// StageNow XML Profile Content Snippet
<wap-provisioningdoc>
  <characteristic type="Clock">
    <parm name="AutoTime" value="true"/>
    <parm name="TimeZone" value="America/Chicago"/>
    <parm name="NTPServer" value="time.google.com"/>
  </characteristic>
  <characteristic type="DevAdmin">
    <parm name="ScreenLockType" value="None"/>
  </characteristic>
</wap-provisioningdoc>
key_takeaways: 2D barcodes can compress large amounts of configuration data into a single scan.
StageNow works on factory-reset devices straight from the shipping box without network pre-configuration.
Exported MX XML can be pushed remotely through EMM OEMConfig to update in-field fleets.

quiz.question: What technology allows Zebra Android devices to process configurations encoded inside a StageNow barcode?
quiz.explanation: Zebra Mobility Extensions (MX) is the system-level firmware layer on Zebra Android devices that parses and executes StageNow configuration instructions.

quiz.question: What file format does Zebra StageNow use internally to represent Mobility Extensions (MX) configuration profiles?
quiz.explanation: Zebra MX configuration profiles are XML documents parsed by the on-device MX framework to configure Wi-Fi, scanner parameters, display settings, and app permissions.

quiz.question: What is the benefit of a StageNow 2D PDF417 or QR barcode over manual device setup?
options: A single scan can configure Wi-Fi, download the latest EMM agent, apply security certificates, and enroll the device in under 60 seconds
quiz.explanation: A single StageNow barcode triggers automated staging, reducing manual device onboarding time from 30 minutes to under 1 minute.

lessons.name: Module 4: Shift-Worker Shared Device Check-In
lessons.summary: Shared device check-in/check-out architectures, badge NFC tap auth, user session wiping, and multi-user profiles.

details.overview: In 24/7 logistics and healthcare environments, devices are shared across multiple consecutive work shifts. Check-in/Check-out (CICO) architectures allow shift workers to tap their employee badge, receive a customized device profile with their credentials, and return the device to the charging rack at shift end for automated cache wiping.
topics: Shared Device Architecture: Check-In / Check-Out (CICO)
NFC badge tap authentication and SSO token injection
Automated post-shift sanitization: Clearing browser cookies, app cache, and temporary scan files
Tracking device custodianship to eliminate misplaced or lost warehouse hardware
lab_guide: Step 1: Configure a Shared Device profile in the EMM console.
Step 2: Set the initial screen to a locked login prompt with NFC badge listener.
Step 3: Simulate shift worker badge tap and verify personalized profile application.
Step 4: Check in the device and confirm that the previous user session data is completely scrubbed.
key_takeaways: Session scrubbing guarantees shift workers cannot see medical or financial data processed by the prior worker.
CICO tracking pinpoints the exact employee who last possessed a damaged or missing scanner.
Single sign-on tokens should have auto-expiration limits matching shift durations.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason for running automated cache wiping when a shift worker returns a shared device?
options: To purge confidential customer or patient data and clear personal session tokens before the next employee logs in
To delete the camera lens software
To speed up the internet download of videos
quiz.explanation: Automated cache wiping on shared devices protects security and privacy by ensuring the subsequent worker starts with a clean application state without leftover session data.

quiz.question: In a 24/7 retail or logistics shift-worker environment, what is the best practice for shared device check-in/check-out?
options: Using NFC badge tap or barcode badge scan to authenticate the worker, assign user profiles, and automatically wipe temporary cached data upon shift end
Letting all workers share the same root password and personal photos
Never cleaning device data between shifts
quiz.explanation: Enterprise shared device check-in (like Zebra Identity Guardian or Workspace ONE Launcher) wipes session data upon logout and re-provisions for the next shift worker.

quiz.question: Which protocol or feature prevents previous worker data (PII, customer signatures) from lingering on a shared device?
options: Automated session logout and app cache wiping / multi-user container reset
quiz.explanation: Shared device management frameworks automatically wipe app data caches, browser cookies, and temporary photos when a worker checks out at shift conclusion.

lessons.name: Module 5: Battery Health & Fleet Lifecycle
lessons.summary: Smart battery telemetry, cycle count degradation alerts, hot-swap battery workflows, and spare pool staging.

details.overview: Battery failure during an active retail or logistics shift halts operations. Smart rugged batteries incorporate internal microcontrollers that report live cycle counts, battery health percentage, temperature history, and estimated capacity degradation to the EMM platform.
topics: Smart battery telemetry: Cycle count, State of Health (SOH), impedance, and temperature history
Hot-swap battery workflows: Swapping batteries within 60 seconds without rebooting the OS
Automated replacement threshold alerts (e.g. SOH < 80% triggers procurement dispatch)
Spare pool staging and charging cradle cycle rotation best practices
lab_guide: Step 1: Query Zebra smart battery parameters using terminal or OEMConfig sensor.
Step 2: Identify batteries with cycle counts exceeding 500 full charge cycles.
Step 3: Test a hot-swap battery procedure: verify the screen stays alive in low-power standby during swap.
Step 4: Build a dashboard report classifying fleet batteries into Healthy, Degraded, and Replace.
details.commands_configs:
// Querying Zebra Smart Battery Telemetry
$ adb shell dumpsys battery
$ adb shell cat /sys/class/power_supply/battery/cycle_count
$ adb shell cat /sys/class/power_supply/battery/health_percentage
key_takeaways: Lithium-ion batteries typically lose 20% of capacity after 500 full charge cycles.
Hot-swap capabilities save minutes per worker by avoiding long Android cold boot sequences.
Proactive battery replacement prevents sudden mid-shift scanner shutdowns.

quiz.question: What does a "Hot-Swap" battery feature allow a warehouse worker to do?
options: Swap a depleted battery with a fresh one without powering down the device or losing their active application state
Heat up the battery on cold winter mornings
Transfer battery power into their smartphone
quiz.explanation: Hot-swap utilizes an internal supercapacitor or backup battery that maintains RAM and CPU power for 60–90 seconds while the main battery is replaced, avoiding reboots.

quiz.question: What battery telemetry metric is critical for identifying aging lithium-ion batteries before they fail on the warehouse floor?
options: Battery Cycle Count and State of Health (SOH) percentage
The color of the plastic case
The brand of the charger cable
quiz.explanation: State of Health (SOH) and cycle count track battery degradation; when SOH falls below 80%, batteries struggle to sustain full shifts and should be cycled out.

quiz.question: What feature on enterprise rugged scanners allows workers to swap an exhausted battery without rebooting the OS or losing session data?
quiz.explanation: Hot-swap technology uses a supercapacitor or backup battery that maintains RAM and CPU state for 60-120 seconds while the worker swaps in a freshly charged battery.

intune-essentials.name: Intune & Endpoint Security
intune-essentials.description: Microsoft Intune architecture, Conditional Access compliance, Windows Autopilot zero-touch deployment, Defender for Endpoint, and Attack Surface Reduction.

lessons.name: Module 1: Endpoint Architecture & Cloud Enrollment
lessons.summary: Microsoft Entra ID join vs hybrid join, Intune service architecture, MDM auto-enrollment scopes, and licensing.

details.overview: Microsoft Intune is the cloud-native endpoint management component of Microsoft Endpoint Manager. Built natively on Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory), Intune governs Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, and Linux devices from a unified cloud console.
topics: Microsoft Entra ID Join vs Hybrid Entra ID Join vs Entra Registered
Configuring automatic MDM enrollment scopes in the Entra admin portal
Intune licensing prerequisites (Microsoft 365 E3/E5, Business Premium, Intune Suite)
Tenant status, cloud service health, and connector configurations
lab_guide: Step 1: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center and navigate to Mobility (MDM and MAM).
Step 2: Configure Microsoft Intune MDM User Scope to "All".
Step 3: Staged enroll a Windows 11 endpoint using an enterprise work account.
Step 4: Verify in the Intune portal that the device registers as "Microsoft Entra joined" and "Managed by Intune".
details.commands_configs:
// Windows Command Line Enrollment Check
$ dsregcmd /status

+----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Device State                                                         |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------+
             AzureAdJoined : YES
          EnterpriseJoined : NO
              DomainJoined : NO
               Device Name : W11-FINANCE-092
key_takeaways: Microsoft Entra ID Join is recommended for all new cloud-first PC deployments.
Hybrid Entra Join should only be maintained if on-premises legacy Kerberos/Active Directory dependencies exist.
Automatic enrollment links Entra identity join directly to Intune MDM provisioning.

quiz.question: What command-line tool verifies Microsoft Entra join and MDM enrollment status on a Windows endpoint?
quiz.explanation: `dsregcmd /status` outputs the comprehensive identity state, showing whether AzureAdJoined is YES and whether Intune tenant MDM URLs are bound.

quiz.question: What is the modern cloud identity provider required for Microsoft Intune device enrollment and conditional access?
options: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory)
quiz.explanation: Microsoft Intune is natively integrated with Microsoft Entra ID to authenticate users, issue PRTs (Primary Refresh Tokens), and enforce device compliance.

quiz.question: Which Windows enrollment option connects a remote worker's personal PC to corporate apps while maintaining privacy?
options: Microsoft Intune MAM (Mobile Application Management) without enrollment
Domain join to local physical cable
quiz.explanation: MAM without enrollment (MAM-WE) protects corporate data inside approved apps (Word, Teams, Outlook) without requiring full device management of the personal PC.

lessons.name: Module 2: Conditional Access & Compliance Policies
lessons.summary: Zero Trust enforcement, device compliance policies, device risk levels, and Conditional Access grant controls.

details.overview: Conditional Access is the Zero Trust policy engine of the Microsoft cloud. It evaluates signals (user identity, location, device compliance status, and Microsoft Defender risk level) and enforces decision controls (Allow, Require MFA, Require Compliant Device, or Block).
topics: Zero Trust principle: "Never trust, always verify, assume breach"
Intune Compliance Policy rules: Minimum OS, BitLocker, Firewall, Antivirus, Secure Boot
Configuring Conditional Access Grant Controls: "Require device to be marked as compliant"
Evaluating What-If scenarios in the Conditional Access troubleshooter
lab_guide: Step 1: Create an Intune Compliance Policy for Windows: Require BitLocker and Antivirus enabled.
Step 2: In Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, create a policy targeting "Office 365" cloud apps.
Step 3: Grant control: Select "Require device to be marked as compliant".
Step 4: Attempt to sign into Outlook from an unmanaged personal PC and confirm access is blocked.
key_takeaways: Conditional Access prevents attackers with stolen passwords from accessing cloud data on unmanaged machines.
Compliance state is calculated continuously by the Intune management extension agent.
Defender for Endpoint feeds real-time machine risk scores directly into compliance evaluation.

quiz.question: What is the role of Conditional Access in a Microsoft Zero Trust security architecture?
options: It evaluates real-time signals (user, device compliance, risk) and enforces access decisions before granting access to corporate cloud resources
It sends monthly paper bills to employees
quiz.explanation: Conditional Access acts as the gatekeeper, verifying that the user and endpoint meet security baselines (such as being an Intune-compliant device) before granting entry to cloud apps.

quiz.question: How do Microsoft Entra Conditional Access and Intune Compliance work together to protect cloud data?
options: Conditional Access checks the Intune compliance flag (e.g. BitLocker encrypted, antivirus active); if non-compliant, access to Microsoft 365 is blocked
quiz.explanation: Conditional Access policies require "Require device to be marked as compliant", ensuring endpoints meet Intune health standards before accessing cloud apps.

quiz.question: What happens when an Intune compliance policy grace period expires on an endpoint with outdated antivirus signatures?
options: The device is marked Non-Compliant and Entra ID Conditional Access blocks corporate access until remediated
The operating system is upgraded to Linux
quiz.explanation: Once the grace period expires, the device is flagged as non-compliant, triggering Conditional Access blocks to protect enterprise resources.

lessons.name: Module 3: Windows Autopilot & Hardware Hashes
lessons.summary: Extract hardware hashes, OEM device registration, user-driven deployment profiles, and Enrollment Status Page (ESP).

details.overview: Windows Autopilot transforms PC staging from hours of manual IT imaging to a zero-touch cloud experience. When a new laptop is turned on by an employee at home, Autopilot detects its hardware hash, binds it to the corporate tenant, joins Entra ID, installs enterprise apps, and configures BitLocker automatically.
topics: Extracting hardware hashes via PowerShell script (Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo)
OEM partner registration (Dell, Lenovo, HP shipping directly to end-users)
Autopilot Deployment Profiles: User-Driven vs Self-Deploying (Kiosk)
Enrollment Status Page (ESP) configuration to block desktop access until critical apps install
lab_guide: Step 1: On a test physical or virtual machine, extract the 4K hardware hash CSV.
Step 2: Upload the CSV into Microsoft Intune > Devices > Windows enrollment > Devices.
Step 3: Assign an Autopilot Profile with "User-Driven" mode and standard user account type.
Step 4: Boot the VM to out-of-box experience (OOBE) and observe the branded corporate login.
details.commands_configs:
// PowerShell Command to Extract Autopilot Hardware Hash
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force
Install-Script -Name Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo -Force
Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo.ps1 -OutputFile C:\AutopilotHardwareHash.csv -Online
key_takeaways: Autopilot eliminates the need to build and maintain monolithic Golden Windows OS images.
OEMs can register hardware hashes at the factory before shipping the PC to the employee.
Enrollment Status Page prevents users from working on a half-configured, unencrypted machine.

quiz.question: What script extracts the hardware hash required to register a Windows computer with Windows Autopilot?
quiz.explanation: `Get-WindowsAutopilotInfo.ps1` gathers the hardware hash, serial number, and UUID necessary to register the device in the Microsoft Autopilot cloud.

quiz.question: What unique identifier is extracted from a Windows computer and uploaded to Microsoft Intune for Windows Autopilot registration?
options: Hardware Hash (4K cryptographic hardware identifier generated from motherboard and TPM components)
quiz.explanation: The Windows Hardware Hash contains a cryptographic signature of the device's hardware components, uniquely binding the physical machine to the enterprise tenant.

quiz.question: During Windows Autopilot self-deploying mode for digital kiosks, which component provides hardware-backed tenant authentication without user interaction?
quiz.explanation: Autopilot self-deploying mode uses TPM 2.0 cryptographic attestation to verify the device's physical identity and bind it to the corporate tenant without requiring user credentials.

lessons.name: Module 4: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
lessons.summary: Defender onboarding scripts, automated investigation & response (AIR), live response sessions, and security baseline deployment.

details.overview: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) is an enterprise endpoint detection and response (EDR) platform. Integrated directly into the Windows OS kernel and Intune, MDE provides real-time behavioral protection, cloud threat intelligence, and automated investigation and remediation (AIR).
topics: Onboarding endpoints to Defender for Endpoint via Intune Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) policy
Automated Investigation & Response (AIR) playbooks for automated malware eradication
Live Response sessions: Opening a secure remote terminal into compromised machines
Deploying Microsoft Intune Security Baselines for Windows, Edge, and Office
lab_guide: Step 1: In the Microsoft Defender portal, establish the Intune service-to-service connection.
Step 2: In Intune, create an Endpoint Detection and Response profile and assign it to "All Corporate Laptops".
Step 3: On a test endpoint, run the simulated attack test script provided by Microsoft.
Step 4: Review the alert timeline, process injection tree, and automated quarantine in the Defender portal.
details.commands_configs:
// Simulated Defender EDR Detection Test Script
$ powershell.exe -NoExit -Command "Write-Host 'Testing Defender EDR Detection'; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://example.com/test_malware' -UseBasicParsing"
key_takeaways: Defender for Endpoint is built into the Windows OS; no separate third-party sensor agent is required.
AIR automates tedious forensic analysis, terminating malicious trees and purging bad registry keys.
Security Baselines apply hundreds of vetted CIS/Microsoft security settings in one click.

quiz.question: What is the primary advantage of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint on Windows 11 compared to legacy third-party antivirus agents?
options: It is built natively into the Windows kernel, requiring no heavy external agent software installation
It turns off the internet automatically
It only works when the computer is shut down
quiz.explanation: Defender for Endpoint is natively embedded within the Windows operating system kernel, delivering superior performance, tamper resistance, and zero third-party agent overhead.

quiz.question: How does Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) integrate with Microsoft Intune to automate threat response?
options: MDE shares device risk level (Low, Medium, High) with Intune compliance rules; high-risk infected devices are quarantined automatically
MDE formats the C: drive on detection
MDE sends paper mail to the user
quiz.explanation: Intune integrates with Defender for Endpoint to evaluate Machine Risk Score, automatically revoking access when active malware or credential theft is detected.

quiz.question: Which feature in Microsoft Defender prevents malicious macros and executable code from launching from Microsoft Office applications?
quiz.explanation: Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules block typical malware behaviors such as obfuscated scripts, Office child processes, and credential stealing from LSASS.

lessons.name: Module 5: Attack Surface Reduction & LAPS
lessons.summary: ASR rules for Office and script obfuscation, Windows Local Admin Password Solution (LAPS) cloud backup, and BitLocker key escrow.

details.overview: Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules prevent common malware techniques, such as Office applications launching child processes, obfuscated macro scripts, and credential theft from LSASS. Windows LAPS automatically rotates unique local administrator passwords and escrows them securely in Microsoft Entra ID.
topics: Configuring high-impact ASR rules: "Block executable content from email client and webmail"
Blocking Office applications from creating executable content or child processes
LSASS credential dumping prevention via ASR rule [9e6c4e1f-7d60-472f-ba1a-a39ef669e4b2]
Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) in Microsoft Entra ID
lab_guide: Step 1: Create an Endpoint Security > Attack Surface Reduction policy in Intune.
Step 2: Set "Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem (lsass.exe)" to Block.
Step 3: Configure Windows LAPS policy: Rotate local admin password every 30 days with 16-character complex string.
Step 4: Verify that the local admin password can be retrieved from the device blade in the Entra portal.
key_takeaways: ASR rules stop zero-day ransomware before it executes by blocking dangerous behavior patterns.
Windows LAPS eliminates shared local admin passwords across your workstation fleet.
Always test ASR rules in "Audit Mode" first to verify internal legacy line-of-business macros.

quiz.question: What security problem does Windows LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) solve?
options: It prevents lateral movement attacks by automatically generating unique, randomized local administrator passwords for every machine and escrowing them in the cloud
It sets the same simple password "admin123" on all corporate laptops
It deletes the administrator account completely
quiz.explanation: LAPS ensures every computer has a unique, strong, frequently rotated local administrator password, preventing attackers who compromise one machine from using the same password on other endpoints.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of Windows LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) managed via Microsoft Intune?
options: Automatically rotating unique, complex passwords for the local administrator account on each device and storing them securely in Entra ID / Intune
Setting the password "admin123" on all computers
Deleting administrator rights from all computers forever
quiz.explanation: Windows LAPS eliminates shared local administrator passwords, automatically rotating unique passwords on each machine to prevent lateral movement attacks.

quiz.question: Which encryption technology does Microsoft Intune enforce on Windows endpoints to protect corporate data at rest?
options: BitLocker Drive Encryption with TPM key protection
quiz.explanation: Intune configures BitLocker drive encryption policies, automatically escrowing 48-digit recovery keys into Microsoft Entra ID for secure recovery.
